key_insight: Explicit analytical solutions describe evaporation and near-contact-line flow in cylindrical-cap droplets, with the same local power-law behavior as spherical-cap droplets for contact angles below 90°.
engineering_relevance: These solutions offer simple benchmarks for modeling evaporation-driven contact-line transport in two-dimensional droplet geometries.
method: Extend a slender-droplet approach to arbitrary contact angles without an arbitrary far-field distance.
Use conformal mapping to derive explicit evaporative-flux expressions.
Couple evaporation to internal Stokes flow and analyze the triple-point region.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical verification of the analytical evaporative flux but provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: The model assumes cylindrical-cap geometry and Stokes flow; matching local exponents does not establish full equivalence with three-dimensional droplets.
paper_title: Some analytical solutions for the evaporative flux and the flow inside a sessile droplet in cylindrical-cap geometry
